newsitem.title: UK: UK retail sales fall 0.8 pct in Dec.
newsitem.headline: UK retail sales fall 0.8 pct in Dec.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK retail sales in December.
RETAIL SALES VOLUME DEC NOV (NOV PREL)
Market forecasts had centred on flat retail sales on the month and a year-on-year increase of 3.5 percent.
BY SECTOR (percentage gain, minus indicates fall)

The average weekly non-seasonally adjusted value of retail sales in December was 4.3 billion stg, 1.8 percent up on December 1995. In value terms, retail sales rose by 4.9 percent in the three months to end December on the same period a year earlier.
The ONS said the value of retail sales in 1996 was 5.4 percent higher than in 1995. This compares with a 1.2 percent increase between 1994 and 1995.
The ONS said the December 1996 trading period has shifted in relation to last year due to the five week trading period in January 1996.
The seasonally adjusted data accounted for this change.
